committee.sub: Morning brief · Friday 25 September 2026 · the committee’s read on the 7am numbers

items.text: Sessions fell 18% week on week to 47 from 57 and ad spend was pulled back to $126.82 from $171.23, yet conversions stayed at zero for another week. CTR actually improved to 4.2% from 3.3%, so the creative is doing its job, the funnel after the click is not.

Budget lost share of 22.8% is still well under rank lost of 72.3%, so the budget conversation stays closed, quality and ad rank are the constraint, not spend. Search Console data only runs through 22 Sept, two days behind Thu 24, so this week's visibility numbers are a lagging read.

/ai-automation-agency.html (20 sessions) and the homepage (19) carried almost all traffic. The branded query 'kontrol ai' ranks #1 with 4 clicks, but unbranded terms like procore xero integration and simpro connector sit at position 41 to 51 with zero clicks, so the dedicated SimPRO Xero page (5 sessions) is not yet matching what those searchers type.

Leads stayed at zero and the calculator ticked up to 1 use from 0, still no booking behind it. Direct fell to 10 from 22 and AI Assistant referrals dropped to 0 from 2, while LinkedIn showed its first session (1) since Chris started posting there, real unpaid demand is still thin.

actions.text: Logo and image assets plus keyword-matched RSA headlines for the serving ad groups are still outstanding, get them into the account.
Fix the homepage form so kontrolTrackLead fires on the Formspree confirm rather than before it, the confirm-then-count logic is still pending.
RSA description D1 still claims 13.3 hours of admin per week, update it to match the current site stats.

weekly: sessions fell 18% week on week to 47 from 57 and users dropped to 44 from 56.
the calculator was used once this week versus zero last week, but no booking has followed.
Organic Search nearly doubled to 14 from 7, Direct fell to 10 from 22, AI Assistant referrals dropped to 0 from 2, and LinkedIn logged its first session (1) since Chris began posting.
